title: Hillel (II)
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He still merited to receive from his grandfather, our holy Rabbi, as in Bava Batra 83b: “Hillel asked Rabbi.” Hyman suggests that this Hillel is mentioned in Avot 2:4, which lists “Rabbi says,” then “Rabban Gamliel his son,” and then “Hillel says” — and so is the reading in the Mishnah of the Westerners, “Rabbi Hillel says” — “Do not separate yourself from the community, and do not judge your fellow until you reach his place,” etc. “He too saw a skull floating on the water and said to it: Because you drowned [others], they drowned you,” etc. (By way of conjecture, Hyman suggests that the phrase “he too saw” is used because his ancestor Hillel saw a skull, as cited in Sukkah 53a, where it explicitly says Hillel the Elder; therefore it says that his descendant Hillel also saw and said as his ancestor did; and there the phrase “he too” became corrupted from the Mishnah of Avot.)

He is mentioned several times with his elder brother Rabbi Yehudah Nesia, as in Pesachim 51a, the Jerusalem Talmud there, beginning of chapter 4, and Tosefta Moed Katan, chapter 2: an incident with Yehudah and Hillel, the sons of Rabban Gamliel, who bathed together in Kabul, and the whole province criticized them, saying, “In our days we have never seen such a thing”; Hillel slipped away and went out to the outer chamber and did not want to tell them, “You are permitted.” Likewise they went out in kordakisin on Shabbat and the province criticized them … they removed them and gave them to their slaves. At the beginning of Semachot, chapter 8: an incident with Yehudah and Hillel, the sons of Rabban Gamliel, who went in to Ben Zakkai in Babylonia (Hyman proposes “to Kabul,” and Ben Zakkai is the one mentioned in Chullin 52a, “Ulla said: Ben Zakkai says … Rabbi Yochanan says,” and perhaps he is Rabbi Zakkai of Kabul).

He is likewise mentioned in a baraita in Sanhedrin 99a after Rabbi, where they said: “Rabbi Hillel says: Israel has no messiah, for they already consumed him in the days of Hezekiah”; and Rav Yosef said of him: “May his Master forgive Rabbi Hillel.”

Although he was the younger brother of Rabbi Yehudah Nesia, Hyman suggests that he did not live as long as his brother; therefore he is mentioned only in baraitot, for this was immediately after Rabbi’s death, when it was still the generation of the Tannaim who arranged the baraitot. But his elder brother Rabbi Yehudah Nesia, who lived long, is therefore counted in the first generation of Palestinian Amoraim. Hyman suggests that perhaps he is the Rabbi Hillel mentioned at the end of Terumot, chapter 1, in whose name Rabbi Chananyah spoke.

The book Chikrei Lev, part 1, p. 66, says that the Rabbi Hillel who said “Israel has no messiah” is the Hillel who established the [calendar of] intercalation; Hyman respectfully rejects that identification, for that Rabbi Hillel lived in the year 670 of the Seleucid era (lishtarot), in the time of Abaye and Rava; see his entry.

notes.text: The opening grandfather is RabbiYehudahHaNasi; the later זקנו referring to Hillel the Elder is ancestor, and נכדו descendant, avoiding the false assertion that the Elder was also his immediate grandfather. The skull analogy is explicitly conjectural, not proof of two events. Hyman’s Avot attribution, Kabul emendation, early death and calendar-Hillel separation remain proposed.670Seleucid stays unconverted.

The consulted Sukkah 53a places the skull saying directly after the baraita naming Hillel the Elder. This supports that occurrence, not Hyman’s conjecture that the descendant independently saw a second skull, his Avot attribution, or the proposed relationship among the two passages. His distinction between the grandfather Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi and the ancestor Hillel the Elder remains explicit. The Kabul emendation and possible Zakkai identification, early-death inference, baraita-only argument and calendar-Hillel distinction remain Hyman’s; the year 670 Seleucid is not converted.
